findings.claim: One cutoff for two moves. The plan now says both moves ship in the first release after LAST_ROOT_RELEASE, because both land on agent-audit before it merges to main. It also extends root-release-cutoff's test_cutoff_matches_tags so every tag after the cutoff has packages/kmctl/apm/apm.yml and no apm/apm.yml, and every older tag the reverse. If main cuts a release from the root in between, that test fails and the cutoff moves for both.
findings.anchor: .loop/plans/apm-per-package/README.md (What follows the move, the consumer entry)

findings.claim: Upgrade advice across the cutoff. _update_fix (doctor.py:170-176) now has to give the whole {git, path, ref} entry. The install how-tos and cli-version-floor.md say a move across the cutoff changes the path. The starter's apm.yml.jinja picks the path from kmctl_ref. A doctor test covers a {path: apm, ref: v0.12.2} project on this CLI getting a fix that names path: packages/kmctl/apm. I found no other code that rewrites only the ref: new_entry is the only writer, and the starter's upgrade recipe re-renders apm.yml.jinja.

Touches now include .pre-commit-config.yaml, scripts/sync_antigravity_rules.py, .claude/rules/*.md, .okf/decisions/*.md (including the resource: sources of 0020 and others), manifesto, summary, audit-pipeline, overview, docs/reference/commands.md, and test globs for packages/kmctl/tests, tests and tests/scripts. A fresh grep turns up only comment mentions outside touches (kinds.py:20 and the okf-stop-check.sh fixture header) plus history files (.okf/log.md, .okf/prototypes). None of these breaks when the folder moves.
